clue.text: Number in shower of rain behind a fairly round object, circled by number of muses

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come behind, after, everything else
the four letters for the Muses' count wrap around the pieces before them

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth
fairly means pretty, as in pretty good
a ball is a round object

indicators.note: a shower scatters the letters of rain into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a figure seen in the rain behind a roundish thing, ringed by the Muses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower of' scrambles RAIN into RINA, which comes 'behind' NIN(A PRETTY BALL)E. The definition 'Number' is a song: the puzzle's theme is ABBA songs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ABBA song title; in show business a number is a song or musical item in a performance.

clue.text: Sun dog

definitions.meaning: the sun is something that sets each evening, so whimsically one that sets
an Irish or English gundog breed

explanation.walkthrough: A crossword compiler is also one, so the clue winks at Paul himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun goes down nightly, making it a sinker below the horizon, and the dog is a well-known gundog breed.

clue.text: Super chap on film, builder

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a thoroughly good, reliable fellow
a film is a thin layer, as of dust

explanation.surface: A superhero type appearing in a movie about construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Super chap on film' suggests Superman in the cinema. A brick, in dated British slang, is a thoroughly decent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays bricks is one kind of construction worker.

clue.text: See 28
Number also wearing blazer, less fashionable

indicators.note: the shortened fire is worn around the word for also
less means the fashionable word is taken away from the fire

parts.note: a blazer here is something blazing, a huge fire
in means fashionable, trendy
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone also in a jacket, but the jacket is out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blazer' looks like a jacket but means a raging fire; 'less' takes away the trendy word, and 'wearing' wraps what remains around the word for also.
explanation.definitionFit: An ABBA song title; a number in show business is a song or musical item.

clue.text: Caught by gunshot, huge bully

indicators.note: the letters sit caught within the run of the words gunshot and huge

explanation.surface: A huge bully is hit by a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian or tough who intimidates others is a synonym.

clue.text: In and facing out

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman who is in and facing the bowling
workers who are out have walked off the job in protest

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman facing the bowler is said to be on strike; 'In' and 'out' look like opposites but describe the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter receiving deliveries holds the strike, and striking workers are said to be out.

clue.text: Old scorer, winger by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the word for a winged creature is said aloud, giving a name spelt differently

parts.note: a winger is a creature with wings, a bird

explanation.surface: A veteran goalscorer whose name suggests a footballer on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' and 'winger' suggest football; William Byrd was a Tudor composer, one who writes scores.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd, the sixteenth-century English composer, wrote musical scores long ago.

clue.text: One born to drink in bar, it is dilapidated boozer

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the word for born takes the scrambled letters inside it as if drinking them

parts.note: nee, as in a married woman's maiden name, means born

indicators.note: dilapidated means falling apart, so the letters of bar and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A born drinker propping up a run-down pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dilapidated' scrambles BAR IT into BRIAT; 'to drink in' puts that inside the word for born. 'drink' and 'bar' belong to the surface, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard, someone habitually intoxicated, is a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Beloved number, if multiplied by two

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment for a loved one, like darling
said twice it is the ABBA song ..., ...

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is ABBA songs; this one's title repeats the word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetheart is a near synonym for this endearment, and the ABBA hit doubles the word.

clue.text: Room in grid without margins

indicators.note: the outer edges of the grid word are trimmed away

parts.note: a lattice is a grid of crossed strips

explanation.surface: A room laid out on a grid with no borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grid' hints at the crossword itself; it is a LATTICE losing its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loft or garret, the space just under the roof, is a room.

clue.text: Given up, having declined to hold information back

indicators.note: the word for declined holds the other piece inside

parts.note: abated means declined, lessened

indicators.note: back means the word for information is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered after refusing to withhold information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GEN into NEG, which ABATED holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or relinquish, so the past participle means renounced.

clue.text: Leader of Opposition bitten by cook, a 6

indicators.note: the first letter is held in the jaws of the cooking word

parts.note: to grill is to cook under direct heat

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Opposition

explanation.surface: The opposition leader is savaged by a cook, a real thug.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer of 6 down, THUG; a gorilla is slang for a hired heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hulking hired heavy or bully is called by the name of the big ape in slang.

clue.text: Simplest of hits: number, if multiplied by three

definitions.meaning: in golf, a very short putt conceded without being played
said three times it is the ABBA song ...! ...! ...!

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is ABBA songs; this title repeats the word three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's tap-in is conceded as too easy to miss, and ABBA sang the word thrice.

clue.text: Bit of a writer with taste for old club

parts.note: a nib is the writing tip of a pen
a lick is a small taste

explanation.surface: Part of an author getting a flavour for an old society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned golf iron, roughly a modern nine iron, is an antique club.

clue.text: Untidy and wet, torn blankets left under couch

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece goes under the first

parts.note: a couch can mean a bed

indicators.note: the word for torn covers the letter for left

parts.note: ragged means torn

explanation.surface: Messy and soggy bedding, ripped blankets left beneath a sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blankets' looks like bedding but is the instruction putting L inside RAGGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled describes someone dishevelled and limp, typically from rain.

clue.text: Groomed male maintained houses

indicators.note: the word for maintained houses, contains, the other letter

parts.note: kept means maintained

explanation.surface: A well-groomed man keeps several homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare positive of unkempt means neat and tidy in appearance.

clue.text: Change number, if multiplied by three

definitions.meaning: said three times it is the ABBA song ..., ..., ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like a verb, but it is small coins. The ABBA title repeats the word three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Small change is coins, a form of cash, and the ABBA hit repeats the word thrice.

clue.text: Excessive pointers point

parts.note: needles on dials are pointers
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Too many pointers making one point.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnecessary or superfluous, more than is called for.

clue.text: Uniting words: number, if multiplied by five

definitions.meaning: the vows said at a wedding
said five times it is the ABBA song ..., ..., ..., ..., ...

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is ABBA songs; this title repeats the phrase five times.
explanation.definitionFit: The vow a bride or groom makes in a marriage ceremony joins two people.

clue.text: Pen like that entering mark shortly

indicators.note: the word for like that goes into the shortened mark
the word for mark is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an imprint is a mark
so means like that, in that way

explanation.surface: A pen of that kind leaving a quick mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is a verb, to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen an animal is to shut it in, to confine or lock up.

clue.text: See 22 down
Treatment of pore with dye, producing a poetic tear

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters of pore and dye into a new form

explanation.surface: A cosmetic procedure dyeing the skin's pores leaves someone weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment' suggests a medicine for eyes, but signals the anagram; the definition is the poetic word for a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare used the compound for a teardrop, so it is a literary word for a tear.

clue.text: Brew on tap is over a barrel

indicators.note: a brew is stirred up, so the letters of on tap is are mixed

explanation.surface: Beer on tap comes from a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrel' fits the beer picture, but 'over a barrel' means stuck in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean caught in a tricky predicament with no easy way out.

clue.text: Speech number

definitions.meaning: Martin Luther King's 1963 address in Washington
an ABBA song of the same title

explanation.definitionFit: The famous civil-rights oration of 1963 shares its title with an ABBA song from 1979.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Strike securing hard currency

indicators.note: the word for strike holds the letter firmly inside

parts.note: to bat is to strike
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A strike that wins hard cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard currency' looks like a phrase, but 'hard' is H.
explanation.definitionFit: The baht is the monetary unit of Thailand.

clue.text: Style arising in Havana, legendary

indicators.note: arising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words Havana and legendary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A legendary style emerging in the Cuban capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hidden letters: 'in' is it. In a down clue 'arising' means reading upwards, so NALE turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair or panache, a stylish vigour, is what the word means.

clue.text: Intellectual Australian language not quite right

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the language is dropped

parts.note: Greek is a language

explanation.surface: An Australian thinker's language is slightly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Germaine Greer is the Australian feminist writer and academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch, is a famous Australian-born thinker.

clue.text: Call number, if multiplied by two

definitions.meaning: said twice it is the ABBA song ... ...

explanation.walkthrough: The theme is ABBA songs; this title repeats the word twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To telephone someone is to phone them, and ABBA's early hit doubles the word.

clue.text: Covers I see pulled back, a relative number

indicators.note: pulled back means the two words are read backwards

parts.note: mats are floor coverings
ah is an exclamation meaning I see
a nana is a grandmother, a relative

explanation.surface: Someone sees covers pulled back to find a relation performing a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled back' reverses both of the first two pieces together, giving HASTAM, which ends inside the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ABBA song title, Spanish for see you tomorrow; a number is a song in a show.

clue.text: Six balls each, four more polished off too much

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls bowled
four more than the six already mentioned is ten

explanation.surface: A cricket bowling tally: six balls each, then four more.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries; 'four more' works off the six, giving ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off food is to eat it all up; doing so to excess is gorging.
